title: pericopsis angolensis subsp. laxiflora
intro: Pericopsis angolensis subsp. laxiflora, commonly known as the African yew, is a plant species belonging to the family Magnoliaceae. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties, which can help to protect against diseases such as cancer, diabetes, and infections. The therapeutic actions of Pericopsis angolensis subsp. laxiflora include anti-cancer, anti-diabetic, and anti-microbial actions, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including alkaloids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids. The bioactive constituents of Pericopsis angolensis subsp. laxiflora, including berberine, quercetin, and kaempferol, have been isolated and studied for their potential therapeutic applications.
